out.other_title: Does debate still work when judges hold strong inaccurate priors or cognitive biases?
out.rationale: Michael et al. call for evaluating debate where judges have strong inaccurate priors. Rahman et al. report that under consultancy mainstream-prior judges were less accurate than skeptical ones (OR 0.70, p = 0.11), while under debate accuracy was nearly identical across prior groups (OR 1.10, p = 0.66); neither odds ratio is significant.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate still works when judges hold strong possibly inaccurate priors, for COVID-19 claims

text: Using mixed-effects logistic regressions, the paper reports that under consultancy mainstream-prior participants were less accurate than skeptical-prior ones (odds ratio 0.70, 95% CI [0.42, 1.10], p = 0.11), while under debate accuracy was virtually identical across belief orientation (OR = 1.10, 95% CI [0.71, 1.71], p = 0.66).
title: Prior-belief effects on accuracy: consultancy vs debate mixed-effects regressions
